summary: Streaming chat responses disconnect or stall mid-generation (SSE/WebSocket) for enterprise customer
description:
Issue summary: Multiple streaming chat sessions (SSE and WebSocket) disconnect or stall mid-generation for Acme Analytics users.

Impact: Customer reports 10-30% of streaming responses either cut off before final tokens are emitted or pause indefinitely requiring client reconnects. This impacts production chat product and causes user-visible truncation and degraded UX.

Environment: Dedicated account running in prod-us-east on Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity). Customer is pinned to redwood-2-large.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Open a streaming chat session via SSE or WebSocket to the Redwood endpoint with pinned model redwood-2-large.
2) Send a multi-turn prompt that yields >300 tokens.
3) Observe stream event sequence: tokens arrive, then stream disconnects with no final done event OR the stream stalls (no events for >45s) while server continues to show active inference.

Expected behavior: Streaming session remains open until model emits end-of-generation markers; clients receive final chunk and close normally.

Actual behavior: Sessions disconnect with 5xx or ECONNRESET at client or stall without final token stream; reconnecting resumes new generation but previous response lost.

Logs/IDs: Customer provided sample request ids: rq_6a9f2c, rq_6a9f2d, rq_6a9f2e. Correlated internal trace IDs: trace-2026-02-25-1352 (partial), trace-2026-02-25-1411. Support bucket: #support-acme-41328.
comments: 2026-02-25 13:40 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer reported increased streaming disconnects starting ~2026-02-25 12:00 UTC. Provided sample request ids and client SDK logs. Asked for network traces and server-side request ids.

2026-02-25 14:05 - Marcus Chen (SRE): Collected proxy logs for the provided request ids. Noted several 502/504s from streaming-proxy around the timestamps and some proxy worker restarts. Investigating whether autoscaler triggered a rebalance.

2026-02-25 15:20 - Priya Kapoor (Infra): Observed elevated kernel socket CLOSE_WAIT counts on a subset of serving hosts between 11:45-13:30 UTC. Possible file descriptor leak in streaming proxy process after recent deployment (rev: ab3c9f7). Rolling analysis.
2026-02-25 18:02 - Acme Analytics (Customer): We see users reporting sessions freeze and have to refresh. This is affecting our live chat on east coast. Any ETA on fix?

2026-02-26 09:12 - Marcus Chen (SRE): Reproduced stall locally with pinned model under sustained token output. Stack traces show streaming-proxy hitting a per-connection timeout (45s) followed by abrupt connection close, but model worker kept running and completed generation. Hypothesis: gap introduced by intermittent backpressure in proxy -> worker socket write path, causing proxy to assume client gone and close connection.

2026-02-27 02:30 - Eng Team (Serving Runtime): Noted increased tail latencies in kernel selection during long sequences after recent runtime change (PR #5278). Related to quantized KV-cache path with models producing long output. Creating a rollback candidate for that change.

2026-03-01 05:10 - Marcus Chen (SRE): Deployed hotfix to streaming-proxy to extend per-connection keepalive and hardened write retries. Monitoring metrics; initial signal shows dropped stream rate down from ~18% to ~3% for Acme test traffic.

2026-03-02 12:00 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer confirmed improvement after fix; still seeing occasional stalls (<1%). Open follow-up to validate full rollback of problematic runtime change on a canary before full rollout. Marking ticket In Progress until follow-up complete.
investigation_notes: Timeline: issue started after runtime change (PR #5278) affecting quantized KV cache path. Proxy logs show 502/504 and per-connection timeouts at streaming-proxy; serving runtime experienced increased tail latencies for long generations. Hypotheses: (1) runtime kernel selection regression causing spikes in token latency that exceed proxy streaming timeouts; (2) streaming-proxy insufficient write retry/keepalive leading to premature closes when tail latency is temporarily high. Evidence: correlated trace IDs show model worker completed generation while client observed disconnect; metrics show spike in token latency concurrent with proxy closes. Reproducible with load test that generates >300 token outputs.
resolution: Applied two-step mitigation: (A) rolling hotfix to streaming-proxy (increase keepalive, add write-retry/backpressure handling) deployed 2026-03-01; (B) reverted/rolled back the runtime PR #5278 from serving runtime canary and running targeted canary tests to validate. Post-mitigation results: customer report rate of streaming disconnects reduced to <1% and internal test harness shows stable streams across >1k simulated sessions. Follow-up actions: full postmortem to be posted to Confluence, permanent runtime fix in progress (ENG-7123), extend streaming SLOs and add synthetic canaries for long-token streams.
